title: TSMC Stock Drops 20 Percent From Peak, But AI Demand Tells a Different Story
excerpt: The world's dominant chipmaker is caught between record revenue and a brutal semiconductor selloff — here's what investors watching the AI trade need to know.
body:
• TSMC shares have fallen over 20 percent from their peak as the global chip selloff rattles semiconductor investors, erasing more than $200 billion in market value.
  • Despite the stock decline, TSMC reported record quarterly revenue and raised its 2026 capital expenditure to over $38 billion, signaling confidence in long-term AI demand.
  • The company manufactures over 90 percent of the world's most advanced chips, making it irreplaceable for AI leaders like Nvidia, Apple, and AMD.
  • For Indian tech investors and the diaspora's large presence in the US semiconductor industry, TSMC's trajectory is a bellwether for the entire AI investment thesis.

The World's Most Important Chipmaker Under Pressure

Taiwan Semiconductor Manufacturing Company, the foundry that fabricates over 90 percent of the world's most advanced processors, has seen its stock slide more than 20 percent from its 2026 highs. The selloff, part of a broader rout in semiconductor stocks that has erased hundreds of billions in market value, has forced investors to ask whether TSMC represents a buying opportunity or a warning sign for the AI boom.

The numbers make a compelling case for the former. TSMC reported record revenue of $28.9 billion in the second quarter, beating analyst estimates. The company raised its 2026 capital expenditure guidance to over $38 billion, nearly all of it directed at expanding capacity for AI chips. Its advanced 3-nanometer and 5-nanometer processes are booked solid through 2027, with Nvidia, Apple, AMD, and Qualcomm all competing for allocation.

Why the Stock Is Falling Anyway

The disconnect between TSMC's fundamentals and its stock price reflects three fears weighing on the semiconductor sector. First, the US government's escalating restrictions on chip exports to China threaten to shrink TSMC's addressable market. China accounted for roughly 11 percent of TSMC's revenue in 2025, and further restrictions could cut deeper.

Second, concerns about overinvestment in AI infrastructure have spooked generalist investors. After two years of aggressive spending by hyperscale cloud companies, some analysts question whether the return on AI investment will materialize quickly enough to justify the capital expenditure. TSMC, as the primary supplier of AI training chips, is directly exposed to this sentiment.

"TSMC is essentially the OPEC of advanced semiconductors. Every AI model in the world runs on chips they manufacture."

— Semiconductor Industry Analyst

Third, geopolitical risk around Taiwan remains the stock's permanent overhang. Any escalation in cross-strait tensions between China and Taiwan immediately hits TSMC's valuation, regardless of the company's operational performance.

What Indian Investors Should Consider

For Indian-origin investors in the US — a demographic that is disproportionately represented in the technology sector and in equity investing — TSMC's trajectory matters both professionally and financially. Many Indian tech workers hold semiconductor stocks through 401(k) plans and individual portfolios, while Indian IT services companies like TCS, Infosys, and HCLTech derive significant revenue from chip industry clients.

The Indian government's own semiconductor ambitions, including subsidies for chip fabrication plants in Gujarat and Karnataka, are modeled in part on TSMC's success. A sustained downturn in global chip valuations could slow India's push to attract foundry investment, while a recovery would reinforce the case for India's semiconductor strategy.

What's Next

TSMC's upcoming earnings call and guidance update will be closely watched for signals on AI demand trajectory and China exposure. Bank of America recently reiterated a buy rating, arguing that AI-related semiconductor spending will more than double to $1.7 trillion over the next five years. For long-term investors with conviction in the AI thesis, the current selloff may represent exactly the entry point the market rarely offers for a company of TSMC's strategic importance.
